scope: Read-only web host, current main deployment workflow, official network ranges and public reachability; no firewall, SSH, nginx, certificate, workflow or application change

operatorSsh.effectivePolicy: publickey yes, password no, keyboard-interactive no, authentication methods publickey, root login without-password
operatorSsh.recoveryConsole: Owner-reported root login previously passed on this Droplet and is recorded in PR #301; no subsequent root password or SSH configuration change was found during this preparation

webAndCertificate.listeners: nginx TCP 80 and 443 on IPv4; Cloudflare presents IPv4 and IPv6 edge addresses to visitors
webAndCertificate.http: chatforia.com and www.chatforia.com redirect to HTTPS www.chatforia.com
webAndCertificate.https: www.chatforia.com serves the static site and proxies /api/ to the HTTPS API origin with the previously approved certificate verification enabled
webAndCertificate.originCertificate: Cloudflare Origin CA certificate with apex and wildcard DNS names, valid from 2026-04-12 to 2041-04-08; private key not read
webAndCertificate.localCertbot: No /etc/letsencrypt/renewal directory or Certbot/ACME timer was found on the web host; current origin certificate renewal is not an HTTP-01 process on this Droplet
webAndCertificate.cloudflare: Owner previously confirmed chatforia.com and www.chatforia.com proxied with Full (strict); Cloudflare edge certificate management is separate

githubActions.currentMainWorkflow: deploy.yml is manual workflow_dispatch on a standard ubuntu-latest runner; deploy job installs the stored SSH key, rsyncs to the web Droplet, then runs a separate SSH command that restores env.js and reloads nginx
githubActions.postSshHardeningEvidence: Actual frontend deployment run #623 succeeded after key-only SSH hardening, proving stored runner key access at that time
githubActions.pr301VerifyMode: Branch-only pinned-host verify_ssh job is prepared but was not dispatched; it is not on current main
githubActions.runnerEgress: GitHub-hosted standard runner IPs are dynamic; retaining all-source TCP 22 with key-only sshd preserves the existing deployment path without a paid fixed-egress runner

reachability.directOriginWww: HTTP 200 before a web firewall; TLS verification was intentionally disabled for this diagnostic because the origin uses a Cloudflare Origin CA certificate
reachability.independentFetcherWww: HTTP 521 with no response headers, Ray ID or source location exposed; this conflicts with local IPv4/IPv6 passes and the owner's earlier cellular pass. Cause remains unknown.

digitalOceanFirewall.latestOwnerProvided: No cloud firewall attached to chatforia-web-01; UFW inactive
digitalOceanFirewall.freshControlPlaneReadback: unavailable from assistant access; owner must confirm current attachment before creating or attaching a new rule set

officialCloudflareCidrs: 15 IPv4 plus seven IPv6 source ranges matched the existing ingress-fencing proposal at this preparation checkpoint; refresh immediately before any separately approved attachment

proposedWebRules.inbound: Allow TCP 22 from All IPv4 and All IPv6 for standard GitHub-hosted runners and operator public-key access; allow TCP 80 and TCP 443 from all 22 official Cloudflare CIDRs; no other inbound rule or tag attachment
proposedWebRules.outbound: Allow ICMP, all TCP ports and all UDP ports to All IPv4 and All IPv6, matching the currently unfenced egress behavior
proposedWebRules.attachment: Create complete firewall without a Droplet attachment, review every rule, then under separate approval attach only chatforia-web-01; no production attachment is authorized by preparation

approvalHold: Investigate or explicitly disposition the independently observed www 521 before tightening the web origin; capture a fresh DigitalOcean attachment/rule view and Cloudflare edge evidence. API firewall change is already complete and separate.
rollback: Detach only the newly attached web firewall, returning to the owner-reported no-cloud-firewall baseline; retain the rule snapshot and verify fresh operator SSH, public web IPv4/IPv6 and direct-origin reachability before closing the incident
